summary: Persist user-selected start date on medication orders
description:
Problem
The Start date field in the drug order form is collected from the user but is not included in the Order POST payload. As a result, the selected date has no effect when saving NEW, RENEW, or REVISE medication orders: the backend defaults dateActivated to the current date when omitted, so the user's choice is silently discarded.
Scope
This ticket covers wiring the form's Start date through to dateActivated for NEW, RENEW, and REVISE flows, including the encounter-handling required for the backend's dateActivated >= encounterDatetime and REVISE +1s constraints to hold.
NEW: the user-selected date is sent as dateActivated. The encounter created in the same POST is backdated to the earliest selected date so the encounter constraint holds.

RENEW: posted as a new order with previousOrder, on a freshly created encounter (per backend semantics: a renewal is a new prescription event, not a continuation). The new encounter's encounterDatetime tracks the chosen start date. The form does not inherit dateActivated from the previous order.

REVISE: the user-selected date is sent as dateActivated against the previous order's existing encounter. The date picker enforces a minimum of previous.dateActivated + 1s so the backend's previous.dateStopped = new.dateActivated - 1s computation produces a valid order chain.

DISCONTINUE: unchanged from current main (preserves the original order's dateActivated; no dateActivated sent in payload).

Out of Scope (deferred)
The following are deferred to follow-up tickets or #2973:
Future-dated orders. These are modeled with scheduledDate + urgency ONSCHEDULEDDATE, not by setting a future dateActivated (the backend rejects future values during validation). Belongs to #2973.

Time-of-day picker bug. The picker's minDate uses the visit's exact startDatetime (a Date with time component), but the picker greys out at day-level and the picked Date has time 00:00 in local TZ. So when a visit started at e.g. 09:33, the picker visually allows that day but the picked Date falls before the visit start, causing the encounter POST to fail with Encounter.datetimeShouldBeInVisitDatesRange. Cleanest fix is clamp-on-submit (round picker minDate to start-of-day, then clamp the picked Date to max(picked, visit.startDatetime) and for REVISE also previous.dateActivated + 1s).

Consolidation of orderEncounterType config currently duplicated between esm-patient-medications-app and esm-patient-orders-app into esm-patient-common-lib.

Field label rename ('Start Date' to 'Activation Date'). Deserves separate UX and translation review.

Acceptance Criteria
[x] On NEW, RENEW, and REVISE, the user-selected Start date is sent as dateActivated in the POST payload.

[x] When the field is left at its default, payload behavior is unchanged from current main (no dateActivated sent; backend defaults to now).

[x] DISCONTINUE preserves the original order's dateActivated (unchanged from current main).

[x] buildMedicationOrder does not pre-fill the form's startDate from the previous order's dateActivated for RENEW or REVISE (no silent backdating when the clinician does not touch the date field).

[x] RENEW creates a fresh encounter with encounterDatetime tracking the chosen start date.

[x] REVISE date picker enforces a minimum of previous.dateActivated + 1s.

[x] Tests cover NEW/RENEW/REVISE (date is sent), DISCONTINUE (preserves), buildMedicationOrder regression (RENEW/REVISE do not inherit), and the pure helpers (getEarliestStartDate, getStartDateMinimum, postOrderOnNewEncounter).

Related
Prior PR attempt: #2241

Current PR: #3198

Future scheduling work: #2973

Recent Visit Detection:

No new consultation bill is created

Payment status displays: PAID (for consultation)

Patient bypasses the cashier and proceeds directly to triage/consultation

The system creates a bill for these new services only

Payment status changes to UNPAID (for new services)

Patient must visit the cashier to pay before lab/pharmacy services



No New Services:
If no new services are ordered, payment status remains PAID

Patient completes visit without seeing the cashier


Unpaid Initial Visit:

The outstanding balance from the initial visit remains visible

The new consultation fee is still waived

summary: Enable Refund Requests and Approval for Paid Bills

Refund request captures:
Bill reference

Refund reason (free text or predefined list)


Once requested:
Bill status transitions from PAID → REFUND REQUESTED

Funds are not yet released



Refund Approval
All refund requests require Administrative approval

Admin can:
Approve refund

Reject refund


On approval:
Bill status transitions from REFUND REQUESTED → REFUNDED


On rejection:
Bill status returns to PAID



Cashier Handling
Approved refunds are visible to the cashier

Cashier completes the refund (cash or electronic, per facility policy)

System records refund completion

Refund cannot be processed without prior admin approval


Status Transitions
PAID → REFUND REQUESTED → REFUNDED

PAID → REFUND REQUESTED → PAID (if rejected)


Audit Logging
Who requested the refund

Who approved/rejected it

Date and time of each action


Scenario Workflow
The patient pays for the lab test

Equipment breaks before the sample is processed

Cashier requests refund → status becomes REFUND REQUESTED

Admin approves refund

Bill status updates to REFUNDED

summary: Bill Discount Management with Audit Trail
description:
Enable administrators to apply discounts to patient bills with full traceability. All discounts must capture initiator, approver, amount, justification, and timestamp for complete auditability.
User Story:
As an Administrator, I want a feature to apply discounts to patient bills, so that we can support facility-level financial needs while maintaining full auditability and preventing informal practices.

Functional Requirements:
Access Control and Configuration 
The ability to initiate or approve discounts is restricted to Admin roles only

Discount functionality must be configurable (enabled/disabled) at the facility level

Facilities can enable/disable the discount feature through system settings

When disabled, discount options are hidden from all users, including admins

Cannot apply multiple discounts to the same bill

Cannot apply discount to bills with status: PAID, REFUNDED, CANCELLED


Discount Initiation 
Administrators can apply discounts to bills with a status of PENDING or UNPAID

Discount can be applied as: 
Percentage discount (e.g., 10%, 25%, 50%)

Fixed amount discount (e.g., 500, 1,000)


System validates that the discount does not exceed the bill total

Add "Apply Discount" action button on eligible bills


Every Discount Captures the following Information 
Initiator ID: Admin user who initiated the discount

Approver ID: Admin user who approved the discount (if different from initiator)

Discount value: The percentage or specific amount

Justification: Mandatory reason for discount

Date and time stamp: Automatic capture of when the discount was applied


Invoice and Receipt Display 
Original price: Full amount before discount e.g., 5,000

Discount applied: Amount, e.g., 500

Final amount: Amount due after discount e.g., 4,500


Audit Trail
Bill reference number

Patient name and identifier

Original amount

Discount amount

Final amount

Initiator name and ID

Approver name and ID (where applicable)

Justification reason

Timestamp

summary: fix(billing): implement safe patient display parsing with validation and fallbacks.
description:
Issue
The billing system's patient display parsing assumed a fixed "identifier-name" format with hyphen delimiter. When backend returned different formats (null, no hyphen, or multiple hyphens), patient names appeared as undefined in bills, invoices, and financial reports. This created:
Empty patient name fields in billing tables and receipts,Non-compliant financial documents missing required patient identification,Failed search/filter operations when looking up bills by patient name,Silent failures with no error visibility or logging

Fix
Implemented parsePatientDisplay() utility function that:
Validates patient display string exists before parsing,Handles multiple format variations (standard "ID-Name", no hyphen, null/undefined, multiple hyphens),Returns guaranteed non-undefined values with meaningful fallbacks ("Unknown Patient", "TEMP-ID"),Adds console warnings for observability when unexpected formats detected and Uses defensive parsing with .indexOf() and .substring() instead of unsafe .split()

Otherwise, the column is rendered as blank.

We want to change it so that:
The status column shows the actual status

The primary actions (Check in and Check out) are rendered as buttons, while other actions are rendered as Overflow menu (which already exists), in a new “actions” column.

In the current implementation of the esm-appointments-app, appointment data is cached globally without scoping it to specific patient contexts. As a result, when a user switches between patients, cached data from one patient may be displayed for another. This causes significant privacy concerns, inaccurate appointment displays, and a violation of data protection standards.
Impact:
Risk of exposing sensitive patient information to unauthorized users.

Misleading data could lead to clinical errors, mismanagement of appointments, or incorrect treatments.

Root Cause: The caching mechanism does not associate appointment data with unique identifiers (e.g., patientId), resulting in data leakage across patient records.

summary: `yarn serve` uses incorrect base URL for lazily compiled resources
description:
Repro steps:
In patient-management, run yarn start --sources packages/esm-appointments-app

In patient-chart, go to packages/esm-patient-chart-app and run yarn serve --port 9001

In the browser, use the openmrs devtool to override the patient-chart-app URL to http://localhost:9001/openmrs-esm-patient-chart-app.js

Go to appointments page and attempt to use a workspace from the patient-chart app (the exported visit form)

Result:
404 not found on URL http://localhost:8080/lazy-compilation-using-

summary: Dispensing modal: "Dispense all prescriptions" fires before medication request data has loaded
description:
Summary
The On Prescription Filled modal (src/fill-prescription/on-prescription-filled.modal.tsx) renders as soon as the order basket is signed, but the medication request bundles are fetched asynchronously via usePrescriptionDetails (SWR). While that fetch is in-flight, medicationRequestBundles is an empty array.
If the user (or an automated test) clicks Dispense all prescriptions before the fetch resolves, onConfirm() iterates over an empty array and makes no dispense or fulfiller-status requests. close() is still called, so the modal dismisses silently and the prescriptions are never marked as dispensed.
Steps to reproduce
Open the dispensing app and start a paper prescription.

Fill and sign the order.

In the Dispense prescriptions modal, click Dispense all prescriptions immediately (within ~1–2 s of the modal appearing).

Observe: no MedicationDispense or MedicationRequest PATCH requests are sent; the prescription remains Active.

Root cause
usePrescriptionDetails returns medicationRequestBundles: [] until the SWR fetch completes. The confirm button has no guard against this loading state.
Fix
Disable the Dispense all prescriptions button while isLoading from usePrescriptionDetails is true:
const { medicationRequestBundles, isLoading: isLoadingPrescriptionDetails } = usePrescriptionDetails(encounterUuid);
// ...
<Button disabled={isSubmitting || isLoadingPrescriptionDetails} onClick={() => onConfirm()}>
  {t('dispenseAllPrescriptions', 'Dispense all prescriptions')}
</Button>
This also resolves intermittent e2e test failures where Playwright clicks the button before the data arrives.

summary: Prevent open redirect via unvalidated returnToUrl
description:
Summary:
A security vulnerability exists where the returnToUrl query parameter is not properly validated after login, allowing attackers to redirect authenticated users to external malicious sites.

The current validation only blocks the exact '/' value, meaning any other input—including full external URLs—is accepted. Since navigation uses window.location.assign() for absolute URLs, this results in unintended redirects to attacker-controlled domains.
Impact:
Enables phishing attacks immediately after successful login

Exploitable without authentication

High risk due to trusted post-login context

Potential compromise of sensitive patient or clinical data

Expected Behavior:
Only internal, trusted routes should be allowed

External or malformed URLs should be rejected

Actual Behavior:
Any URL is accepted and used for navigation

Users can be redirected to external sites after login

Root Cause:
returnToUrl is retrieved from query parameters and passed directly to navigation without validation. The navigation mechanism allows absolute URLs, enabling external redirects.
Affected Files:
location-picker-view.component.tsx

location-picker.test.tsx

summary: "Call" action crashes the page when the API request fails
description:
The "Call" action in the queue table sends a request to the server to mark a patient as being called. If that request fails for any reason — network problem, server error, missing configuration — the failure is not handled gracefully.
In a development build, the failure produces a full-screen red "Uncaught runtime errors" overlay covering the page; the user has to reload the page to recover.
In a production build (where the dev-only error overlay is disabled), the same failure becomes silent — the Call button click appears to do nothing. The error is only visible in the browser console, which end users do not look at.
Either way, the user gets no proper feedback (toast, snackbar, dialog) about what went wrong. They either see a developer-targeted crash screen or no feedback at all.
A related, separate-but-connected issue: the Call action sends data to the server without first checking that the required values (queue name, ticket number, status) are present. If those values are missing due to misconfiguration, the same silent/crashing failure path is triggered.
Steps to Reproduce
Open the Service Queues app.

Find a queue entry whose status is the default "waiting" status — the Call button only appears for these.

Open browser DevTools (Cmd+Opt+I) → Network tab.

Change the throttling dropdown from "No throttling" to Offline (this simulates a network failure).

Click the Call button on the queue entry.

Expected: the user sees a clear error message (red toast or snackbar) saying something like "Couldn't call patient — please try again." The page remains usable.
Actual: a full-screen "Uncaught runtime errors: TypeError: Failed to fetch" overlay appears in development. In a production deployment the click would appear to do nothing, with the error only visible in the browser console.
Acceptance Criteria
When the Call API request fails for any reason (network error, server returning an error, missing input), no full-screen crash overlay appears.

The user sees a visible error message (e.g., a red toast/snackbar) explaining the action failed.

The page remains functional — no reload required.

Existing successful behavior (the confirmation modal opening on success) is preserved.

summary: Queue-screen widget polls regardless of user activity

That's 1,200 requests per hour, per open tab. In a real clinic, multiple devices and tabs end up open (a nurse on a workstation, a monitor in the waiting room, a backup browser session a staff member forgot to close). Each one polls independently. Backend load multiplies for no user-visible benefit.
The fix is activity-aware polling: poll faster when someone is actively interacting with the page (focused tab, recent input), slower when idle, and rely on browser focus events for instant refresh when the user returns to the tab.

The polling interval adapts to user activity: faster (5–10 seconds) when the tab is active, slower (30–60 seconds) or paused when idle or in a background tab.

SWR's revalidateOnFocus: true is set so the data refreshes immediately when the user returns to the tab.

summary: Persist medication renewals with action=RENEW (not NEW)
description:
When a clinician clicks Renew on a medication tile, O3 internally tracks the basket action as RENEW but rewrites it to action: 'NEW' before POSTing to the OpenMRS REST API. The new order persists with order_action='NEW' and previous_order_id set, instead of order_action='RENEW'.
This creates three downstream problems:
Reports can't distinguish renewals from new orders by action alone. Any "show me renewal rates / chronic medication continuity" analysis has to follow previous_order_id to reconstruct renewals — and treat them as renewals based on a structural pointer rather than the action field that was designed to carry this signal.

The FHIR layer maps the chain to the wrong field. MedicationRequestTranslatorImpl only populates priorPrescription for REVISE/DISCONTINUE, and basedOn for RENEW. For O3-placed NEW orders with previousOrder set, neither fires — see [FM2-680] for the FHIR-side gap. Sending the correct action removes one half of that interaction.

The wiki's "internal translation in O3" gotcha (Order Entry in O3: A PM Reference §3.2 + §3.5 #1) becomes a permanent documented oddity rather than an artifact of an early implementation choice.

Root cause
packages/esm-patient-medications-app/src/api/api.ts:179 — when the basket item's action is 'RENEW', the prepMedicationOrderPostData function emits action: 'NEW' on the wire. Introduced in PR #2949 under O3-5169 with no documented reason — likely copy-paste from the NEW branch.
Proposed fix
One-line change:
   } else if (order.action === 'RENEW') {
     return {
-      action: 'NEW',
+      action: 'RENEW',
       previousOrder: order.previousOrder,
Backend behavior verification (spike)
Tested live against an OpenMRS 3.6.0 distro:
POST /ws/rest/v1/encounter with action: 'RENEW' and previousOrder set is accepted cleanly — no rejection, no silent coercion.

The persisted row has order_action='RENEW', previous_order_id set.

The FHIR API (with the current translator) populates basedOn for the renewal — better than the current state where neither field fires. Once FM2-680 lands, priorPrescription will populate instead, which is the canonical field per FHIR R4.

OrderServiceImpl.saveOrder behavior is identical between action=NEW (with previousOrder set) and action=RENEW — same auto-stop logic (none for either), same orderable-match check, same active-orders ambiguity check. The rewrite was never needed to satisfy a backend constraint.

Acceptance criteria

summary: Patient search results unmount and remount on every keystroke, causing multi-second UI stalls and heap growth
description:
Symptom
In the patient search (both the compact dropdown and the advanced search page), every keystroke that changes the query causes the entire rendered banner list to unmount and remount. With ~50 accumulated patient banners (e.g. five auto-paginated pages of ten), this:
triggers ~150 simultaneous backend requests (per-banner /obs photo lookup, /visit, /person) within a few ms

blocks the JS main thread long enough that the next keystroke event sits in the event queue for multiple seconds before dispatching

accumulates promise-reaction / SWR-subscriber state in the heap that does not appear to be released

In one captured session, a single keypress took 3.7 s to register as a network request, and three Firefox heap snapshots taken seconds apart showed mCallback edges growing 75k → 153k → 458k.
Reproduce
Open the patient search workspace (compact dropdown is enough).

Type a query that returns many results, e.g. 10.

Scroll the results so the IntersectionObserver auto-paginates a few times (accumulate ~50 banners).

Type one more character and watch DevTools Network + Performance:

   - 100+ simultaneous /obs?patient=…&concept=… and /visit?patient=… requests fire.
   - The new /patient?q=… request is delayed by 1–5 s after the keypress.
Repeat several times and take Memory snapshots; retained heap grows monotonically.

Root cause
useInfinitePatientSearch (@openmrs/esm-patient-search-app/src/patient-search.resource.tsx:83) calls useSWRInfinite without keepPreviousData. When searchQuery changes:
getUrl returns URLs for the new query → SWR sees a new key sequence.

data resets to undefined, isLoading becomes true.

Both view components gate on isLoading and return a skeleton/loader, throwing away the entire results subtree:
compact-patient-search/patient-search.component.tsx:52 → <Loader />

patient-search-page/patient-search-lg.component.tsx:41 → <LoadingState />

Every accumulated <PatientBanner key={patient.uuid}> unmounts, then remounts when the response arrives. Per remounted banner the fan-out is:
PatientPhoto → usePatientPhoto → /obs?patient=…&concept=<photoConceptUuid>&v=full

useVisit(patientUuid) called directly in PatientBanner (patient-banner.component.tsx:41)

VisitTag extension from esm-patient-banner-app → another useVisit(patientUuid)

start-visit-button slot → potentially another useVisit

/person/<uuid> lookups for contact-details / deceased state

Compounding factor: useSWRInfinite's size is not reset on key change. After auto-paginating to size=5, every subsequent keystroke immediately fires five pages of the new query in parallel. Tracked separately in O3-5715.
Proposed fix
Two changes, applied together:
1. Keep previous data during query-change fetches
Add keepPreviousData: true to the useSWRInfinite call in useInfinitePatientSearch:
    
const { data, isLoading, isValidating, setSize, error, size } = useSWRInfinite(
  shouldFetch ? getUrl : null,
  openmrsFetch,
  { keepPreviousData: true },
);
This keeps the banner list mounted across query changes. With stable key={patient.uuid}, React reuses banners for patients still in the new results, so no remount → no fan-out → no main-thread stall. isLoading then stays false on subsequent searches (only true on the very first load), and the loader gates in the view components don't tear down the subtree. isValidating can drive a non-disruptive loading hint if one is desired.
2. Harden the loader gates
Change both view components' loader gates so they only swap in the full skeleton when there is genuinely nothing to show:
compact-patient-search/patient-search.component.tsx:52 — if (isLoading) → if (isLoading && !searchResults?.length)

patient-search-page/patient-search-lg.component.tsx:41 — if (isLoading) → if (isLoading && !results?.length)

The keepPreviousData change above already keeps isLoading false during query-change fetches, but tightening the gate makes the intent explicit ("only show the full skeleton when we have nothing to show") and removes any reliance on SWR's isLoading semantics holding across versions.
Leave the existing next-page indicator (the small <Loading withOverlay={false} small /> at patient-search.component.tsx:94-96) untouched — it fires off hasMore / isValidating, not isLoading, and is the right indicator for auto-pagination.
Evidence
HAR file from 2026-05-28T10:19:28 – 10:23:22 showing 24 patient searches with response-end → first-side-effect-request gaps ranging 20 ms (idle UI) to 5.7 s (stalled UI), with the burst always firing the moment the thread frees.

Three Firefox heap snapshots taken seconds apart showing 141 MB → 161 MB → 181 MB retained, with mCallback, mCreationStack, mIncumbentJSGlobal edge counts roughly doubling per snapshot.

summary: Add a schema-configurable searchable dropdown backed by a live REST endpoint
description:
The problem
A nurse fills in an insurance claim form on behalf of the treating doctor. The claim has to identify the clinician, and the list of eligible clinicians lives in an insurer-maintained directory that changes continuously — people join, leave, and lose accreditation.
Today our forms can't do this well:
Static dropdown choices are fixed when the form is built, so they go stale

Remote choices already exist (remote-select), but each list source must be registered in application code, so connecting a form to a new live list needs a developer and a software release

The first attempt (PR #175, superseded) downloaded the whole list in one request — big lists get cut off, there's no real search, and reopened forms show a code instead of a name. PR #178 is the active implementation.

What we'd build
A built-in data source that a form schema can point at a REST endpoint, so form builders can back any dropdown with a live list without engine or host-app code changes.
Acceptance criteria
Typing sends the entered term through the configured search parameter and displays matching results.

Each result displays its labelKey value; selecting it returns the valueKey value to the existing form control and adapter (an obs question stores it as the obs value, exactly as any select does today).

The initial (empty-term) load requests a bounded page (limit, default 20, overridable) — never the full collection.

Reopening a saved form resolves the stored value and displays its label.

The field works correctly inside existing repeating groups, with independent search and edit-mode resolution for every row. (Repetition itself is the existing repeating mechanism, not this feature.)

Search and resolution failures produce a visible, accessible error state distinguishable from "no matches." Note: today's remote-select collapses errors into an empty list for every data source, so this is a shared-behavior enhancement in the control as well as a data-source requirement — see the implementation contract.

Existing forms and registered data sources behave unchanged, and the library gains no new required provider for consumers (HttpClient must remain optional — consumers that don't provide it keep working, minus this data source).

Focused tests cover option mapping (results-wrapped and bare-array responses), search parameter construction, saved-value resolution, search and resolution failures versus successful empty results (including the visible error state), and the registration/compatibility guarantees in criterion 7.

Implementation contract
Configuration uses the standard questionOptions.datasource: { name, config } schema key and renders through the existing remote-select control. A parallel rendering type or schema key does not satisfy this ticket.

The engine registers the data source itself (working name endpoint) in the shared DataSources registry via optional injection, and only when that name is not already registered. A host-provided implementation therefore takes precedence regardless of initialization order: if the host registered first, the engine defers (the guard); if the host registers later, the registry's existing last-registration-wins overwrite applies. Both directions are test-pinned.

Config keys: endpointUrl (required), labelKey (default display), valueKey (default uuid), searchParam (default q), resultsKey (default results), limit (default 20), limitParam (default limit).

Saved-value resolution convention: GET {endpointUrl}/{urlEncodedValue}, overridable via an optional resolveUrlTemplate config with a {value} placeholder.

The endpoint data source must not convert request failures into an empty successful result; failures propagate to the control. Remote-select distinguishes a request failure from a successful empty response and exposes an accessible error message.

Supported endpoints are browser-accessible HTTP GET endpoints returning JSON (a results-wrapped or bare array). Custom authentication is out of scope: same-origin endpoints may use the existing session; cross-origin endpoints must already be browser-accessible with suitable CORS configuration. Relative URLs are the portability norm (to be documented). GraphQL and POST search are out of scope.

Where the selection is stored — answered
The earlier open questions to the implementing team have been resolved, and the DHA HIE docs corrected two premises:
All selectable clinicians exist as OpenMRS providers; the form stores the provider UUID.

Regulator details (licence number, licensing body) live as provider attributes synced from the registry; the claim resolves them at build time — a standard claim identifies exactly one doctor by practitioner_identification_number + practitioner_regulation_body.

Doctor approval exists only for emergency (ECCIF) claims and is run by the HIE via OTP; standard claims have no approval step.

None of that changes this ticket's mechanism — it's recorded so the claims form design consuming this feature doesn't re-open it.
Not in scope
The encounter-provider enhancements (multiple providers, configurable roles) — separate ticket; this feature is its search mechanism

The eligible-providers endpoint and licence re-validation at claim build — claims module

Claim generation or submission

The React form engine equivalent

summary: Capture and surface diagnosis certainty (confirmed / provisional)
description:
Background
Every diagnosis saved through the visit note form is presumed by fiat: the form provides no certainty control and hardcodes certainty: 'PROVISIONAL' on each diagnosis it saves (createDiagnosis in visit-notes-form.workspace.tsx). The backend stores certainty per encounter diagnosis (enum CONFIRMED / PROVISIONAL), and other writers such as REST clients may set CONFIRMED, but the primary authoring flow cannot.
Nothing displays the field either. The DiagnosisTags styleguide component renders only the diagnosis name and a rank-based color (red for primary, blue for secondary). The encounters table resource fetches certainty into its row model but no component renders it, and the visits widget representation does not fetch it at all.
The distinction between a confirmed and a provisional diagnosis is clinically meaningful, and a field that is neither captured nor displayed cannot carry it.
Proposal
Add a certainty control to the visit note form so clinicians can mark each diagnosis confirmed or provisional, using the backend's own terms (which also match FHIR's Condition.verificationStatus). Needs design input.
Display certainty wherever diagnosis tags are rendered. Tag color already encodes rank, so options for design review:
A text suffix, for example "Diabetes mellitus (provisional)". Survives colorblindness, screen readers, and printing. Confirmed diagnoses stay unmarked so the common case adds no noise.

An outline (vs. filled) tag treatment for provisional diagnoses.

A tooltip or accessible description only.

Scope
Visit note form in esm-patient-notes-app: add the certainty control and stop hardcoding PROVISIONAL.
DiagnosisTags in esm-core's styleguide (separate esm-core PR).
Add certainty to the visits widget representation in esm-patient-chart so visit-level rollups have the data. The encounters table representation already fetches it.
Extend the dedupeDiagnoses helper (added in O3-5822) with specified aggregation rules for duplicates of the same concept across encounters of one visit: identity is the concept UUID or exact non-coded text; rank is the minimum across duplicates (primary if primary in any encounter); certainty is the strongest across duplicates (confirmed if confirmed in any encounter). Document and test both rules. The result is a display-level aggregate: it retains one contributing record's uuid (as a stable key), display, and diagnosis reference, while rank and certainty are aggregates that may not match that record. It must not be treated as an encounter diagnosis.
Open questions
Visual encoding for certainty on tags, pending design input.
Whether tag length is a concern in dense visit rows with several diagnoses.
Whether existing PROVISIONAL data should be labelled as provisional once display lands, given it was recorded without clinician choice.

summary: Starting a visit from a patient search result throws because the patient-chart workspace group is launched without group props

can't access property "patientUuid", e.groupProps is null

The framework then renders the group's action menu, passing groupProps = null to every patient-chart action-button icon, and VisitForm reads its patient context only from groupProps. summary: Emit precompressed (gzip -9 and brotli) assets from openmrs build and serve them statically
description:
Background
In the reference application, compression happens on-the-fly at the gateway at gzip's default level 1, per request, on the gateway's CPU — and deployments not using the reference gateway serve entirely uncompressed (the frontend image's nginx has no compression directives; measured: the 3.19 MB styleguide CSS ships raw). Measured on real assets: gzip-1 → gzip-9 is 22–28% less transfer (CSS 232 kB → 166 kB; largest JS chunk 310 kB → 243 kB), and brotli/zstd save a further ~25% beyond gzip-9. Paying the compression cost once at assemble time is strictly better than paying a worse version of it on every request.
Requested change
openmrs assemble (or the shared build config) emits precompressed siblings for compressible assets (js/css/json/svg/html): .gz at maximum level and .br.

File a follow-up PR against openmrs-distro-referenceapplication enabling gzip_static in frontend/nginx.conf (and brotli static serving where the nginx image supports it — note stock nginx lacks the brotli module, so this may require an nginx image change) with pass-through at the gateway (already-encoded responses are not re-compressed).

Evaluate gzip_static always (not shipping raw compressible files in the image): gzip support in clients is effectively universal, and this substantially shrinks the image — at the cost of confounding tooling/analysis that reads raw files from the image. Document the decision either way.

Acceptance criteria
Assembled output contains .gz and .br siblings for all compressible assets.

Serving the frontend image directly returns compressed responses for clients sending Accept-Encoding (verify with curl; content-encoding header present, transfer size matches the precompressed file).

Before/after transfer sizes for a representative page load recorded on this ticket.

Follow-up distro PR/ticket filed and linked.

Automated test in the CLI package covering precompressed-sibling emission.

commits.subject: (feat) O3-5872: Add support for static compression of frontend (#1838)

summary: Change language modal and user menu language item crash with RangeError when allowed locales include a region
description:
The REST session endpoint reports locale and allowedLocales in Java's Locale#toString() form (en_US, sw_KE, pt_BR). These are not valid BCP 47 language tags, and Intl.DisplayNames throws RangeError rather than degrading when handed one. Two components in the primary navigation app pass these values to Intl.DisplayNames unnormalized, so on any deployment whose allowed locale list carries a region, both crash. The app ships regional translation bundles (en_US, sw_KE, pt_BR, zh_CN and more), so these are supported configurations, not edge cases.
Steps to reproduce
Set the locale.allowed.list global property to include a regional locale, e.g. en, en_US, sw_KE

Log in and set the session locale to en_US

Open the user menu in the top nav

Click Change next to the language item

Observed behavior
The user menu's language item crashes as soon as the menu opens when the session locale is regional (new Intl.DisplayNames([session.locale], …) throws RangeError: Invalid language tag: en_US)

The change language modal crashes on open when any allowed locale is regional, for the same reason (change-language.modal.tsx, languageNames memo)

Root cause
change-language.modal.tsx builds Intl.DisplayNames from each entry of session.allowedLocales raw

change-language-link.extension.tsx builds it from session.locale raw

The framework only normalizes underscores when setting document.documentElement.lang (setUserLanguage in esm-api/src/current-user.ts); it never writes the normalized value back to the session store and never touches allowedLocales, so both fields reach these components in underscore form

Verified against the backend: SessionController1_9 adds Context.getLocale() and getAllowedLocales() as raw Java Locale objects, which serialize via toString() to underscore form.
Secondary issue (same modal): the last locale in a long list is invisible
With enough allowed locales (observed with 14), the last entry in the modal is invisible while still being clickable. .languageOptionsContainer has a max-height with no overflow-y, so the list overflows into the ModalBody, which becomes the scroll container and receives Carbon's cds--modal-scroll-content fade mask. The mask keeps the bottom of the body faded even at maximum scroll, so the final locale (Italiano on a 14-locale install) never becomes visible. Neither checkVisibility() nor hit-testing flags it, since masks affect neither. Verified live against a local instance; fixed by scrolling the container itself and clearing Carbon's fade band with an end margin.
Related
The same modal also swallows failed update requests (handleSubmit neither awaits nor catches), leaving the spinner stuck with no error shown; the fix for this crash addresses that alongside it since both live in the same file.
Out of scope: POSIX-style variants such as uz@Latn can be displayed once normalized, but cannot be submitted at all — the session POST parses the value with LocaleUtils.toLocale, which rejects both uz@Latn and uz-Latn. Supporting those needs a backend change in webservices.rest.

commits.subject: (fix) O3-5874: Handle regional locales in the change language modal (#1832)

summary: Prevent render crashes on incomplete FHIR demographics/coding data across medications, orders, vitals, and tests
description:
Several patient chart widgets may crash at render time when patient or observation data is incomplete.
The issue occurs when code accesses array index 0 and then reads a nested property without guarding the indexed value. In real hospital data, empty arrays are common (for example no registered address, or missing coding entries), so this creates intermittent but high-impact UI failures.
Problem Statement:
Affected areas include medications, orders, vitals, and test-results print/table flows.
Widgets may throw runtime TypeError during render when:
patient address exists as an empty array

identifier coding exists as an empty array

observation code coding exists as an empty array

When this happens, clinicians may lose visibility of key chart sections for affected patients.
Clinical and Operational Impact:
Critical patient information may fail to render during care workflows.

Print and review workflows can break for valid-but-incomplete records.

Trust in EMR reliability is reduced due to patient-specific crashes.

Root Cause:
Unsafe nested property access after array indexing in render-path logic.
Optional chaining was not applied to the indexed element itself.
Scope of Fix:
Add safe optional chaining at all vulnerable access points in impacted widgets so missing data resolves gracefully to empty or undefined display states rather than crashing.

summary: Support fullWidth configuration for obs-by-encounter-widget
description:

Reference: routes.json#L13

summary: Patient registration: Wait for deletions before reporting a successful save

summary: Make automatically generated patient identifiers retry-safe
description:
Impact
Retrying a partially completed save can consume multiple generated identifier values. When editing an existing patient, it can also attach duplicate identifiers.
For a new patient, retries waste generated values but do not attach duplicates. Once the patient exists, the retry goes through PatientResource1_8.update, which only applies the person block and ignores the identifiers array.
Affected code
packages/esm-patient-registration-app/src/patient-registration/form-manager.ts

packages/esm-patient-registration-app/src/patient-registration/form-manager.test.ts

Root cause
Each save attempt generates identifiers again. The save transaction remembers whether the main patient request succeeded, but it does not remember generated values or successful identifier additions.
Newly added identifier fields have no identifierUuid (initializeIdentifier never sets one), so every retry POSTs to /patient/{uuid}/identifier without a uuid and the REST resource creates a new row each time.
Each call to /idgen/identifiersource/{uuid}/identifier writes a log entry and advances the sequence, so every retry consumes a value.
If a later operation fails, retrying repeats identifier work that already completed.
Reproduction
Edit an existing patient.

Add an identifier configured for automatic generation.

Submit the form.

Allow the identifier request to succeed, then make a later operation fail.

Retry the submission.

Another identifier is generated and attached to the patient.
Expected behavior
Retrying the same submission should reuse the generated value and should not repeat an identifier addition that already succeeded.
Implementation direction
Extend the save transaction state to retain generated identifier values and completed identifier additions, keyed by a stable identifier field key.
Use serializable records rather than Set or Map. The transaction manager is stored inside _patientRegistrationData for offline synchronization.
Retry only operations that did not complete successfully.
Note on offline: esm-core's sync (processHandler in esm-offline/src/sync.ts) only writes lastError back to IndexedDB on failure. It never persists the mutated item content, so no transaction state (including today's patientSaved) survives between sync runs. Fixing that belongs in esm-core and is out of scope here. Offline mode is also disabled in the reference application (supportOffline: false), so the online retry path is what matters.
Acceptance criteria
A generated identifier is generated once across retries of the same submission.

A successful identifier addition is not repeated.

A failed identifier addition is retried.

New-patient retries do not consume another generated value.

Existing-patient retries do not attach duplicate identifiers.

The transaction state is made up of plain serializable objects (no Set or Map).

Add tests that fail a later operation and then retry with the same transaction state.

Verified against openmrs-esm-patient-management commit c64fb336. Still applies at e23ce30c; the only change to form-manager.ts since is O3-5913 (awaiting identifier deletions), which does not touch identifier generation.

commits.subject: (fix) O3-5916: Reuse generated identifiers when retrying a patient save (#2780)

summary: Keep newly added relationship rows correctly associated
description:
Impact
When multiple relationships are added, removing one row can cause another row to display a relationship type that does not match its Formik value.
Affected code
packages/esm-patient-registration-app/src/patient-registration/section/patient-relationships/relationships-section.component.tsx

packages/esm-patient-registration-app/src/patient-registration/patient-registration.types.ts

packages/esm-patient-registration-app/src/patient-registration/section/patient-relationships/relationships-section.test.tsx

Root cause
New relationships do not have server UUIDs, but the UUID is used as the React key. Multiple new rows therefore share the same undefined key.
The relationship type selector uses defaultValue, making it uncontrolled. When React reuses a row after another row is removed, the selector can retain state from the removed row.
Reproduction
Add two new relationship rows.

Select a different person and relationship type in each row.

Remove the first row.

Inspect the remaining row.

Its displayed selection may not match its Formik value.

Expected behavior
Each relationship row should retain its own person and relationship type when other rows are added or removed.
Implementation direction
Give each new relationship a stable client-side identifier when it is created. Use the server UUID as the key for existing relationships and the client-side identifier for new relationships.
Make the relationship type selector controlled by its Formik value. Do not include the client-side identifier in REST payloads.
Acceptance criteria
Every relationship row has a unique, stable React key.

The relationship type selector is controlled by Formik.

Removing one row does not change another row’s displayed or stored values.

Adding multiple rows produces no duplicate-key warning.

Add an interaction test that assigns different values to two rows, removes the first, and verifies the second.

Verified against openmrs-esm-patient-management commit c64fb336.

summary: Allow birth and death on the same calendar day

summary: Clear stale death metadata when marking a patient alive
description:
Impact

Affected code

packages/esm-patient-registration-app/src/patient-registration/patient-registration.types.ts
packages/esm-patient-registration-app/src/patient-registration/form-manager.test.ts

dead remains true, and the previous death metadata remains.

deathDate, causeOfDeath, and causeOfDeathNonCoded are explicitly null.

FHIR continues to represent the patient as not deceased.

Add a unit test for the generated payload.

summary: Expose person attributes on the form-entry patient object
description:
The O3 form engine currently exposes a limited set of patient properties to form logic — most notably age and sex/gender — which authors can reference inside JavaScript expressions for conditional rendering, calculated values, and validation (e.g. patient.age >= 18, patient.gender === 'female').

summary: Renewing a medication files the renewal encounter in the original order's closed visit
description:
Renewing a medication from the chart opens the order basket with the original order's visit as the workspace's visit context. If that visit is closed, the renewal encounter is created inside it and its datetime is clamped into the old visit's window. A renewal made today ends up filed under a visit from months ago, while the renewal order itself is activated today.
This is a regression from the Workspace v2 migration (O3-4961, openmrs-esm-patient-chart#2800). Before that, Renew launched the basket through the same visit check as Add. Affects patient-chart 12.0.0 onwards.
Steps to reproduce (visits enabled, RDE not needed)
Pick a patient with a medication ordered in a visit that is now closed and older than dispensing's expiry window (medicationRequestExpirationPeriodInDays, 90 by default).

Start a new visit for the patient today.

Active medications > Actions menu > Renew. Save the basket.

Check the visit history and Dispensing > Active prescriptions.

Expected
The renewal encounter lands in today's visit and the renewal shows up in Active prescriptions.
Actual
The encounter sits in the closed visit, dated to it. Dispensing filters Active prescriptions by encounter date, so the renewal is missing there and only appears under All prescriptions. Today's visit shows no prescribing activity. Recording: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6ff1ab4-230d-485f-9c8b-50979c048f73 
Core accepts this. OrderValidator only rejects an encounter dated after the order's activation, so nothing on the backend flags a September order in an April encounter.
Cause
handleRenewClick in esm-patient-medications-app's medications details table builds the workspace group props from the medication's own encounter.visit and passes them when launching the order basket. The basket signs through postOrdersOnNewEncounter in esm-patient-common-lib, which creates the encounter in whatever visit it's handed and clamps the datetime into a closed visit's window.
Fix
Route Renew through useStartVisitIfNeeded and open the basket without the medication's group props, so it uses the chart's current or selected visit. PR: https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart/pull/3619 
Two things this depends on or leaves open:
The start-visit prompt path never resolves after a visit is created, because the visit-form workspace drops the onVisitStarted callback the dialog passes it. That predates this ticket and already affects Add. Tracked separately (ticket to follow).

Discontinue and Modify launch the basket the same way and probably need the same treatment. Needs verifying first.

Not the fix
Changing which activation date postOrdersOnNewEncounter pins the encounter to (the earliest/latest swap this ticket was originally titled for) only moves the timestamp inside the wrong visit, and in a mixed basket rewrites other orders' dates. The order dates are already right; the visit is wrong.
Encounters already filed this way are not repaired by the fix.

commits.subject: (fix) O3-5953: Use the active or selected visit when renewing medication orders (#3619)

summary: MUAC color code not set for patients aged exactly 5, 10, or 18
description:
In getMuacColorCode (packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/vitals-biometrics-form/vitals-biometrics-form.utils.ts), the age-bracket boundary conditions are inconsistent between color cases within the same bracket.
For example, in the 0-5 age bracket, the "red" case uses age <= 5, but the "yellow" and "green" cases use age < 5. This means a patient exactly 5 years old with a healthy MUAC value (e.g. 13cm) gets no color code at all.
More critically, patients exactly 10 or 18 years old get NO color code set for ANY MUAC value, because:
The "5-10" bracket uses age > 5 && age < 10 (excludes 10)

The "10-18" bracket uses age > 10 && age < 18 (excludes both 10 and 18)

The "18+" bracket uses age > 18 (excludes 18)

Verified via unit test: calling getMuacColorCode(10, 20, callback) or getMuacColorCode(18, 20, callback) never invokes the callback, regardless of MUAC value.
Fix: make all brackets consistently inclusive on the lower bound (age <= 5, age > 5 && age <= 10, age > 10 && age <= 18, age > 18), so there's no gap at the boundary ages. Fix + regression tests ready; full esm-patient-vitals-app test suite (72 tests) passes.

commits.subject: (fix) O3-5957: Correct MUAC color code age boundaries (#3626)

summary: Queue location is blank when the login location is not queue-tagged

When creating a queue entry in the Service Queues app, the Queue Location field remains blank if the login location is not queue-tagged, even when it has a queue-tagged ancestor.
The Service Queues dashboard correctly resolves and selects the nearest queue-tagged ancestor. The form still defaults to the login location, which isn't among its dropdown options, leaving the field blank.

summary: Remove unreferenced SCSS files and the dead AllergyFormTab component from the patient chart

summary: Form engine never loads Angular locale data: the locale import requests .mjs files that do not exist
description:
Background
FeWrapperComponent in @openmrs/esm-form-entry-app lazily imports Angular locale data through a webpack context restricted to .mjs. @angular/common/locales/ ships only .js files, so the context is empty, dist/assets/l10n/locales/ is never emitted, and the import rejects on every form launch with Cannot find module './en.mjs'.
registerLocaleData() has therefore never run. The engine falls back to Angular's built-in en-US data, so dates and numbers in every form are formatted as US English regardless of the user's locale.
Requested change
Point both the webpackInclude and the request at .js, and narrow the include so it matches only what can actually be requested — the code always uses the two-letter base language (language.substring(0, 2)).
A bare /\\.js$/ matches all 1,731 files in that directory and emits roughly 2.6 MB of lazy chunks to serve at most thirty locales; anchoring on the path separator is both smaller and closer to the intent. Note that webpackInclude is tested against the resolved path rather than the request, so a ^\\./ anchor will silently match nothing.
Acceptance criteria
Launching a form under a non-English supported locale registers that locale's data, and dates and numbers render using it.

No Cannot find module rejection is logged on form launch in any supported locale.

The build emits only locale chunks that can be requested, not the full CLDR set.

Automated tests cover that the locale import resolves for a supported non-English locale, that the rejection path is not hit, and that an unsupported locale degrades without throwing.

commits.subject: (fix) O3-5976: Fix Angular locale import requesting non-existent .mjs files (#3657)

summary: Unhandled rejections pass a raw Error into the toast description, which React cannot render
description:
Background
esm-error-handling's global handlers pass their raw argument straight into the toast:
window.onunhandledrejection = function (event: PromiseRejectionEvent) {
  dispatchToastShown({ description: event.reason ?? '…', kind: 'error', title: 'Error' });
};
event.reason is normally an Error, and it reaches the toast's subtitle as an object. React cannot render an object as a child, so the toast fails to render and takes its subtree down with it — meaning the user sees nothing at all for an error that was meant to be surfaced to them.
Observed while running the Angular form engine without zone.js, where a previously swallowed rejection became a real unhandledrejection. The console showed Invalid prop 'subtitle' supplied to 'ActionableNotification', expected a ReactNode followed by Objects are not valid as a React child (found: [object Error]).
window.onerror alongside it takes the same shape and should be checked for the same problem.
Requested change
Coerce whatever arrives to a string before it reaches the toast — the module already has ensureErrorObject(), whose .message is the natural choice — so that any rejection reason produces a readable notification instead of an unrenderable one.
Acceptance criteria
An unhandled rejection whose reason is an Error produces a toast showing its message.

The same holds for a reason that is a string, a plain object, null or undefined.

No React rendering error is produced in any of those cases, and the toast subtree survives.

window.onerror is covered by the same handling.

Automated tests cover each reason shape above.

commits.subject: (fix) O3-5981: Coerce error reasons to strings before showing the error toast (#1888)

summary: Saved image attachments are missing when editing a visit note
description:
An image uploaded through a visit note saves successfully and appears on the patient's Attachments page, but it is missing when we reopen that note for editing.
Steps to reproduce
On https://dev3.openmrs.org, open a test patient with an active visit.

Add a visit note with a primary diagnosis, note text and one PNG image.

Click Save and close. Confirm the image appears on the patient's Attachments page.

Go to Visits, expand the visit and open Timeline.

Open the saved Visit Note encounter's actions menu and select Edit this encounter.

Actual behaviour
The note text and diagnosis reload. The Image section contains only Add image, with no saved thumbnail.
Expected behaviour
Images uploaded through a visit note should remain associated with that encounter and appear when the note is reopened for editing.
Validation
Reproduced on dev3 on 16 September 2026 with Tiny Test and the note text "QA attachment test: single PNG upload, 16 September 2026." The single image saved successfully before reopening the note. This is separate from the concurrent-upload failure tracked in ATT-65.
Investigation
The visit-note form calls createAttachment with the patient UUID and uploaded file. The shared helper sends no encounter UUID, although AttachmentResource.upload accepts an encounter parameter and ComplexObsSaver assigns it to the attachment observation.
The edit form also starts with an empty images array and does not load saved attachments. Linking uploads alone will not populate the edit form.
Proposed scope
Pass the saved visit-note encounter UUID when uploading its images.

Load attachments associated with that encounter when editing the note.

Keep saved attachments separate from new uploads so a text edit does not upload existing images again.

Preserve existing patient-level attachments on the Attachments page. Do not infer a note association for older attachments that were saved without one.

Acceptance criteria
Create a note with one image, save it and reopen it: the saved image is visible.

Edit only the note text and save: the existing image remains and is not duplicated.

Add another image while editing and save: both images appear when the note is reopened.

Attachments from other encounters are not shown as belonging to this note.

Related historical work: O3-2618 wired visit-note uploads into the patient Attachments page. It did not specify loading those images when editing the note.

commits.subject: (feat) O3-5986: Let attachments be recorded on and read by encounter (#1887)
(fix) O3-5986: Show a visit note's saved images when editing it (#3668)

summary: Attachment upload dialog ignores the caller's allowed extensions and reports "Upload complete" before anything is uploaded
description:
The visit note form's Add image dialog accepts PDFs even though the form asks it not to, and tells the user the file was uploaded when it hasn't left the browser yet.
Steps to reproduce
On dev3 or a local stack, open a patient with an active visit.
Open the visit note form and click Add image.

Switch to Upload files. The helper text reads "Supported files are jpeg, jpg, png, pdf."

Drop a PDF, name it and click Add attachment.

Actual behaviour
The PDF goes through to the review step. A green toast says "Upload complete: consent.pdf uploaded successfully". The note form shows a blank square with a remove control where a thumbnail should be. Nothing has been sent to the server at this point; the actual upload only happens on Save and close. If the note is saved, the PDF is stored as a note attachment and never shows in the note's Image section again.
Expected behaviour
The dialog only offers the file types the caller allows, so a PDF is refused in the visit note form the same way a .txt is. The "Upload complete" toast is only shown when a file has actually been uploaded.
Investigation
The visit note form passes allowedExtensions to the capture-photo-modal with pdf filtered out (visit-notes-form.component.tsx). That prop is declared in camera-media-uploader-types.ts but nothing reads it. camera-media-uploader.component.tsx, media-uploader.component.tsx and file-review.component.tsx each call useAllowedFileExtensions() themselves, which fetches the backend attachments.allowedFileExtensions property, and the wrapper overwrites the context value with that result. So the caller's list has no effect.
The toast comes from upload-status.component.tsx, which shows "Upload complete" as soon as the caller's saveFile promise resolves. In the visit note form saveFile only appends the file to form state and resolves.
Proposed fix
The dialog honours the allowedExtensions it is given and falls back to the backend list only when the caller passes nothing. The helper text and the file input's accept list follow the same list.

The success toast becomes the caller's responsibility, or the dialog takes a flag saying whether saveFile actually uploads.

Found while working on O3-5986. Related: O3-5988 (size limit), O3-5989 (partial save in the visit note form).

commits.subject: (fix) O3-5987: Let callers restrict the attachment dialog's file types and quiet its upload toast (#3673)

summary: Attachment upload dialog shows a file size limit that is unrelated to the backend's attachments.maxUploadFileSize
description:
The Add attachment dialog tells the user "File limit is 1MB" and refuses larger files client side, but that number is the attachments app's frontend config default. The backend enforces its own limit from the attachments.maxUploadFileSize global property, and the two never see each other.
Steps to reproduce
On a local stack with attachments.maxUploadFileSize at its default of 5.0:
Open the visit note form, click Add image, switch to Upload files. The dialog says "File limit is 1MB".

Drop a 2.9 MB PNG. The dialog refuses it: "The file "big.png" exceeds the size limit of 1 MB."

Then set attachments.maxUploadFileSize to 0.5 and repeat with a 0.8 MB PNG:
The dialog accepts it and moves to the review step.

POST /ws/rest/v1/attachment with the same file returns 400 "The file exceeds the maximum size".

In the visit note form the second case surfaces after the note itself has been saved, which is O3-5989.
Expected behaviour
The limit the dialog shows and checks is the limit the server enforces. An implementer changes one property and both sides follow.
Investigation
media-uploader.component.tsx reads maxFileSize from attachments-config-schema.ts (default 1) for both the helper text and the client-side check. The server checks ctx.getMaxUploadFileSize() in AttachmentResource.upload. The dialog already reads the allowed extensions from the backend property through useAllowedFileExtensions, so the size limit is the odd one out.
One caveat for the reference distro: the nginx gateway has no client_max_body_size set, so nginx's 1 MB default rejects larger uploads with a 413 before they reach the module. That matches the frontend default by coincidence. Raising the backend property alone won't help on the reference distro until the gateway limit is raised too, which is worth a note in the distro docs or a matching gateway setting.
Proposed fix
Read attachments.maxUploadFileSize the same way the extensions are read (a small hook in esm-patient-common-lib next to useAllowedFileExtensions), use it for the helper text and the check, and deprecate the maxFileSize frontend config key so there is one source of truth.
Found while working on O3-5986. Related: O3-5987 (allowed extensions and early toast), O3-5989 (partial save in the visit note form).

commits.subject: (fix) O3-5988: Use the backend attachment upload limit (#3683)

summary: Visit note form leaves a saved note behind when an image upload is rejected, and saving again creates a duplicate
description:
If the server rejects one of the images in a visit note, the note and its diagnoses are already saved, but the form stays open as if nothing was saved. Pressing Save and close again creates a second visit note.
Steps to reproduce
Open a patient with an active visit and start a visit note. Add a diagnosis and some note text.

Click Add image and pick a file the server will reject. A text file renamed to .png works: it passes the dialog and the server refuses it for its content type.

Click Save and close.

Actual behaviour
A red toast says "Error saving visit note: The file content type text/plain is not allowed". The form stays open with the title "Add visit note" and everything the user typed. A visit note encounter with the text and diagnosis already exists on the server. Clicking Save and close again creates a second encounter with the same text and diagnosis. Reproduced on a local stack: one rejected upload, two notes, zero images.
Expected behaviour
Either the note is treated as saved and the user is told which images did not upload, or a retry updates the note that already exists. In no case should a second note be created.
Investigation
onSubmit in visit-notes-form.component.tsx is a promise chain: create or update the encounter, then delete and recreate diagnoses, then upload each image with createAttachment. The catch handler only shows the toast. Nothing rolls back, and the form still believes it is creating because isEditing is derived from the launch props and never changes after the encounter is created. The second submit posts a new encounter.
Any server-side rejection the dialog doesn't catch first leads here: a content type mismatch, a size limit lower than the dialog's (O3-5988), a denied file name, or an image that fails to decode.
Proposed fix
Two reasonable shapes:
After the encounter is created, switch the form to editing that encounter, so a retry updates it and only re-sends the failed images.

On a partial failure, close the workspace as saved and show a warning naming the images that didn't upload, so the user adds them again from the note.

The first keeps the user's context, the second is simpler. Either way the reproduction above becomes the regression test.
Found while working on O3-5986, which links uploaded images to the note's encounter and makes the half-saved state easier to notice. Related: O3-5987, O3-5988.

commits.subject: (fix) O3-5989: Keep a visit note saved when one of its images is rejected (#3670)

summary: Let users remove an image already saved on a visit note without deleting the note
description:
O3-5986 makes the visit note form show the images already saved on the note when we edit it. Those saved images are read only on purpose: there is no way to remove one from the form. This story adds that.
Why there is no remove control today
The attachment removal endpoint, DELETE /ws/rest/v1/attachment/{uuid}, can also void the encounter when it has no obs left. A visit note whose text is blank has no other obs, and its diagnoses hang off the encounter rather than being obs. Reproduced on a local stack: deleting the only image of a text-less note voided the note encounter and took the diagnoses with it. A remove button wired to that endpoint would let someone delete a visit note by accident from the image section.
Expected behaviour
Removing a saved image should behave like editing the rest of the note. In local testing, immediate removal left Save and close disabled, which made it unclear whether the change had been saved. We're making removal part of the draft instead.
Remove marks the saved image for removal and enables Save and close. No delete request is sent yet.

Show that the image will be removed when the note is saved, with an Undo action.

Undo cancels the pending removal. If nothing else has changed, Save and close returns to disabled.

Discard cancels pending removals along with the other unsaved changes. Closing with pending removals uses the workspace's unsaved-changes guard.

Save and close applies the removals. Use DELETE /ws/rest/v1/obs/{uuid} to void only the image obs, preserving the encounter and its diagnoses.

Removing images alone should not rewrite the note or its diagnoses.

If a removal fails, keep the editor open with a clear error and allow retry. Do not repeat successful removals. If part of the save has already succeeded, make that clear; Discard cannot undo changes already saved by that attempt.

Refresh the encounter and visit data, the encounter-scoped attachments list the form reads, and the patient-level list the Attachments page reads after successful removals.

Tests
Remove stages the change without a delete request and enables Save and close.

Undo returns an otherwise unchanged form to clean; Discard makes no delete request.

Saving removes only the selected image obs. The encounter and its diagnoses survive, including a note with blank text and one image.

Removing images alone does not rewrite the note or upload images.

A failed removal keeps the editor open. Retrying skips images already removed successfully.

Out of scope
Removing images added in the current session before saving already works; they only live in form state.
The Attachments page's own delete behaviour is unchanged. This story uses obs voiding specifically to preserve the visit note and its diagnoses.
Related: O3-5986 (shows the saved images), O3-5989 (partial save when an upload is rejected).
Implementation: PR #3684.

summary: Starting or selecting a visit from the visit prompt doesn't continue to the workspace that asked for it
description:
When a chart action needs a visit and the patient has none, useStartVisitIfNeeded shows a visit prompt and waits for the user to start or pick a visit before continuing. Neither path continues today. After the visit is started or selected, the workspace the user asked for doesn't open, and they have to click the action again.
This affects 17 hook calls across 11 files in the medications, orders, vitals, notes, forms, and chart apps, via useLaunchWorkspaceRequiringVisit and useStartVisitIfNeeded.
Cause
There are two problems:
With RDE off, the "No active visit" dialog passes onVisitStarted into the start-visit-workspace-form workspace, but the chart's wrapper for that workspace (visit-form.workspace.tsx) never reads it. The promise never resolves. Before the Workspace v2 migration (O3-4961, openmrs-esm-patient-chart#2800), this path didn't pass a callback at all, so this has never worked.

With RDE on, selecting a visit resolves the promise straight away. But setting a new visit context makes the chart relaunch its workspace group once the visit is refetched, and launchWorkspaceGroup2 closes every open window when the group props change. The resumed workspace gets closed before it renders. The RDE-off path hits the same thing once the callback is wired up.

Steps to reproduce
Open a patient with no active visit.

Medications > Record active medications.

RDE off: click Start new visit, then fill in and save the visit form. RDE on: select a visit and click Continue.

Expected: the medication ordering workspace opens.
Actual: nothing opens. The banner shows the visit, and clicking Record active medications again opens Add drug order.
Reproduced on dev3 (patient-chart main) on 2026-09-23 for both paths. For RDE, holding back the chart's refetch of the selected visit makes the workspace appear at about 440 ms and disappear right after the refetch lands, which confirms the relaunch closes it.
The RDE-off behaviour is present in every release, including RefApp 3.5.0 (patient-chart 11.3.0), 3.6.0 (12.1.0) and 3.7.0 (12.3.4). The RDE-on behaviour is present from patient-chart 12.0.0 (RefApp 3.6.0 and 3.7.0).
Fix
The chart's visit form wrapper accepts onVisitStarted and calls it after updating the visit context.

The patient chart store records which visit the chart's workspace group was last launched with. The chart sets it after each successful relaunch.

useStartVisitIfNeeded resolves true only once that matches the new visit context, for both the RDE and RDE-off paths. Under RDE, closing the switcher after a selection no longer resolves false.

Tests cover the wrapper forwarding the callback, the chart recording the relaunched visit, the visit check waiting on each path, and the switcher resolving false when closed without a selection.
Out of scope
Cancelling. Closing the dialog or discarding the visit form leaves the promise pending. No caller treats false differently from pending, and the form can't see the workspace header's Close button, so there's no reliable way to report every cancel. openmrs-esm-patient-chart#3619 adds dialog cancel handling.

"Create new visit…" in the RDE switcher. It closes the switcher, which resolves false, then opens the visit form with no callback, so it also doesn't continue. We should track that separately.

Related
openmrs-esm-patient-chart#3619 (O3-5953) edits the same block in useStartVisitIfNeeded, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase. Renew picks up this fix once both are in.

commits.subject: (fix) O3-5998: Continue to the requested workspace after starting or selecting a visit (#3688)

summary: Retrying a failed lab result save creates duplicate results on the order
description:
Saving lab results from the Enter test results workspace makes three separate requests: it posts the result obs to the order's encounter, discontinues the test order, then sets the order's fulfiller status to COMPLETED. Each request commits on its own. If the second or third one fails, the results are already saved, but the order isn't COMPLETED, so the form stays in create mode with the value still filled in. Clicking Save again posts the obs a second time.
Reproduction
Reproduced on a local stack (core 2.8.10-SNAPSHOT, webservices.rest 3.5.0) with patient-chart main:
Open a test order with no results and choose Add results.

Enter a value and save, with POST /order (the discontinue) failing. An "Error saving lab results" toast shows and the workspace stays open.

Save again.

The order ends up COMPLETED with two identical, non-voided result obs.
Why
POST /encounter/{uuid} with obs adds rows and never replaces them. EncounterResource1_8.setObs clears the encounter's obs set in memory, but Encounter.obs is mappedBy = "encounter" with no orphan removal, so the existing rows stay. saveEncounter inserts every obs that has no id, and nothing checks for an existing result on the same order.

Repeating the discontinue returns a 500 (CannotStopInactiveOrderException) once the order is stopped, with the default order.allowSettingStopDateOnInactiveOrders=false.

The fulfiller update is safe to repeat.

So if the fulfiller update is the request that fails, or the discontinue commits but its response is lost, every retry adds another copy of the results and then fails on the discontinue. The order can never be completed from the form.
Expected behaviour
Saving the results and discontinuing the order should succeed or fail together. The encounter endpoint accepts inline orders and saves them in the same transaction as the obs, the same way the order basket sends discontinue orders.

If an order already has saved results but isn't COMPLETED, the form should show the saved values, update those obs on save, discontinue the order only if it's still active, then mark it as fulfilled.

A failed save should refetch the saved results so the next attempt sees them.

Tests
Results and the discontinue go in one encounter request, followed by the fulfiller update.

The fulfiller update isn't sent when saving the results fails.

The discontinue is skipped when the order is already stopped.

A failed save refetches the saved results.

An order with saved results gets those obs updated, not new ones posted.

Implementation: PR #3692.

summary: Prevent loss of unsaved medication dosage entries when switching dosage modes
description:
When entering a medication order, switching from structured dosage to free-text dosage clears the entered dose, unit, route, frequency, and patient instructions. Switching back clears the free-text entry. An accidental switch therefore requires clinicians to re-enter their work.
Preserve each mode’s unsaved entries independently while the form remains open. Show only the selected mode’s dosage fields and submit only that mode’s dosage representation.
Current behavior
When a clinician enters a structured dosage (for example: dose, unit, route, frequency, instructions) and then switches to free-text dosage mode, the structured values are lost.

When they switch back, the free-text entry is also lost.

This forces them to re-enter information repeatedly, which slows down medication ordering and increases the risk of data entry errors.

If a save fails, the entered values are not preserved consistently, making retry attempts more frustrating.

Expected behavior
Structured dosage details and free-text dosage entries should be preserved independently.

Switching between dosage modes should retain the data already entered in each mode.

Only the fields relevant to the currently selected mode should be visible/active at any given time.

Draft values should be cleared only after a successful save, not when the save fails.

Clinicians should be able to switch modes freely without losing medication order context.

Acceptance criteria
Switching modes and back restores the values entered in each mode.

Inactive dosage details are hidden from the form and medication header.

Free-text submissions exclude structured dose, unit, route, frequency, and patient instructions.

Structured submissions exclude free-text dosage.

Failed saves preserve entered values for retry.

Tests cover switching in both directions, display isolation, submission filtering, and failed-save preservation.

Impact
This improves medication order entry efficiency, reduces user frustration, and prevents loss of clinical information during routine prescribing workflows.

commits.subject: (fix) O3-6019: Preserve medication dosage drafts when switching modes (#3639)

summary: Every form downloads WHO growth reference data even when it doesn't use it
description:
Description
The form engine ships a set of WHO reference tables used to calculate child growth z-scores (weight-for-age, height-for-age, BMI-for-age). These tables are large (roughly 1.3 MB) and are currently bundled into the code that loads whenever any form is opened. As a result, every form open in the patient chart downloads and parses this data, regardless of whether the form has any growth calculations in it. In practice almost no forms in the reference application or common distributions use these helpers, so this is pure overhead on every form load, which hurts most on slow connections and low-end devices.
Separately, forms that do use these calculations should have the reference data in place before any default values or expressions are evaluated, and should handle the case where the data fails to load without silently producing wrong or missing results.
Acceptance criteria
Opening a form that has no z-score calculations does not download or parse the WHO reference tables.

Opening a form that does use z-score helpers loads only the reference data that form needs.

Z-score results are identical to current behaviour for all inputs (both sexes, all age bands, out-of-range and missing values).

Z-score helpers continue to work in compound expressions (comparisons, ternaries, Number() wrapping), including in calculate expressions.

Default values and expressions are not evaluated until required data has finished loading. This applies to subforms and to re-opened forms where other data is already cached.

If required data fails to load, the form shows a clear error with a way to retry, and initial values, expressions, and submission (including submission triggered externally) stay blocked until the retry succeeds.

Values the user has already entered are not lost when the form re-renders.

Measured startup bundle size for the form engine app is materially reduced.

Related PR
https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-form-engine-lib/pull/824

commits.subject: (chore) O3-6025: Add missing form engine translation keys (#3754)

summary: Vitals and biometrics chart view shows a loading spinner and causes layout jump on first switch
description:
Description
The vitals and biometrics widgets load their chart code lazily, so the first time a user switches from the table view to the chart view, there's a delay while the chart code downloads. During that delay the widget shows a single-line loading indicator, which collapses the card to one row. Widgets below it jump up, then get pushed back down when the chart appears. This is noticeable on slower connections and is disorienting, especially for keyboard users where focusing and activating the switcher happen almost together.
The delay itself is also avoidable in most cases: the chart code could be ready by the time the user actually clicks, since there's a clear signal of intent beforehand (hovering or focusing the switcher).
Acceptance criteria
Hovering over or focusing the table/chart switcher begins preparing the chart view so that, in the common case, clicking it shows the chart with no visible loading state.
