When the chart is not yet ready, the loading placeholder matches the height of the final chart view so the card and the widgets below it do not shift.

The loading placeholder remains accessible to screen readers (announced as loading / progress).

Applies to both the vitals widget and the biometrics widget.

Card height is identical in loading state and rendered state.

summary: Login location picker ignores the configured number of locations to load
description:
Description
The login app has two settings for the location picker on the login screen: one to control how many locations are fetched at a time (chooseLocation.locationsPerRequest) and one to control how many are shown (chooseLocation.numberToShow). Neither setting actually does anything. The picker always fetches 50 locations per request regardless of what an implementation configures, so changing these values in a distro config has no effect.
numberToShow is left over from an older fixed-length location list and no longer has a meaningful equivalent now that the picker uses infinite scroll, so keeping it in the config only misleads implementers.
Acceptance criteria
When chooseLocation.locationsPerRequest is set in config, the login location picker uses that value for each batch of locations it fetches and for when it loads more on scroll.

When it isn't set, the picker keeps its current default behaviour.

chooseLocation.numberToShow is no longer offered as a config option. Implementations that still set it see at most a standard "unknown config key" warning, with no other change in behaviour.

No visible UI changes to the login screen.

Covered by a test that verifies the configured value reaches the location picker.

summary: Remove the legacy workspace (v1) system from the framework
description:
Description
O3 currently carries two workspace systems side by side: the original workspace system (v1) and its replacement (workspace v2). Keeping both adds maintenance cost, makes the framework harder to understand for contributors, and leaves two different ways for apps to open side panels and forms.
The old v1 system should be removed from the framework. This is a breaking change: any app still opening or registering workspaces through the v1 API will stop working once it's gone. Some parts of the patient chart and patient management apps still rely on the old API, so they need to move to v2 before this can land.
Acceptance criteria
All v1 workspace code and APIs are removed from the framework.

All first-party O3 apps (including patient chart and patient management) use workspace v2 only, with no remaining references to the v1 API.

Workspaces in the reference application open, close, and behave as before after the removal.

App route definitions are still validated correctly, including the workspace v2 entries.

Framework and storybook mocks are updated to reflect the removed APIs.

The change is clearly marked as breaking in release notes, with guidance for implementers and third-party apps on migrating to workspace v2.

summary: Forms that calculate growth z-scores can't be saved in the Angular form engine
description:
In the Angular form engine (esm-form-entry-app), the z-score helpers take the WHO reference data as their first argument, e.g. calcWeightForHeightZscore(weightForHeightRef, height, weight). AMPATH's POC triage form uses all three. The app never provides weightForHeightRef, heightForAgeRef or bmiForAgeRef. So as soon as the user enters a height or weight, the expression fails and the z-score field is set to false.
The form still passes validation, and the encounter payload sends value: false for each z-score obs. The backend rejects that for a numeric concept with a 400 (For input string: "false"), so the form can't be saved. I reproduced this with ngx-formentry 20.0.1-pre.582 and got the 400 from a local backend.
AMPATH's ng2-amrs adds these references to the patient data source in getPatientObject. O3's version of getPatientObject leaves them out.
Expected behaviour
A form that uses weightForHeightRef, heightForAgeRef or bmiForAgeRef gets the WHO reference data for the patient's sex and age. The data is chosen the same way as in ng2-amrs, so the z-scores match.

When no reference data applies to the patient (aged 18 or over, sex other than F or M, or no birth date), the reference is null rather than missing, so the field isn't set to false.

Forms that don't use the references don't download the tables. Forms that do load only the tables the patient needs. O3-6025 did the same for the React form engine.

Existing form schemas work without changes.

Related: O3-6025

commits.subject: (fix) O3-6044: Provide WHO z-score reference data to the Angular form engine (#3753)

summary: Share one Back button across patient chart workspaces
description:
Several patient chart workspaces copy the same Back button markup and SCSS. We should replace those copies with one shared WorkspaceBackButton in esm-patient-common-lib.
This came up in review on openmrs-esm-patient-chart#3745, which adds another copy for clinical forms.
What I found
These workspaces use identical .backButton SCSS and the same renderIcon={(props: ComponentProps<typeof ArrowLeftIcon>) => <ArrowLeftIcon size={24} {...props} />} line:
Drug order: add-drug-order.component.tsx, add-drug-order.scss

General order: add-general-order.component.tsx, orderable-concept-search.scss

Test order: add-test-order.component.tsx, add-test-order.scss

Clinical forms: form-entry.component.tsx, form-entry.scss (from #3745)

Patient list details and the task list use close variants with different spacing. The task list's Back button switches views inside the workspace instead of closing it.
Most of that SCSS works around Carbon's Button. Carbon renders renderIcon after the button's children and gives the icon the cds--btn__icon class, which sets its margin and fill. So each copy uses order to move the arrow in front of the label, and !important to override that margin and fill.
The copies also pass iconDescription, but it does nothing here. Carbon only uses it as the label on icon-only buttons. On these buttons it passes it to the icon as aria-label, and the framework's ArrowLeftIcon drops it.
Proposed fix
Add a WorkspaceBackButton to esm-patient-common-lib that takes a label and an onClick. Render the arrow as a child before the label instead of through renderIcon. That should let us drop the order rules and the !important overrides, since nothing would add the cds--btn__icon class. Then move the workspaces above onto it and delete their local .backButton styles.
How we'll check it
Each Back button looks the same as it does today on desktop and tablet: arrow before the label, same spacing, same hover and focus styles.

Each Back button does what it does today, including the unsaved-changes prompt where the workspace has one.

The button's accessible name is its translated label.

None of the migrated apps keep local .backButton styles.

Out of scope
Having core's Workspace2 draw a Back control for child workspaces itself. It already knows whether a workspace is a child, but that's a design change for every app that uses workspaces.

The trendline's "Back to timeline" button in test results. It's in a page header rather than a workspace, and it wraps the button in a link.

summary: `extractVariableNames()` drops variables and returns nested arrays for expressions inside arrow functions
description:
Background
extractVariableNames() in @openmrs/esm-expression-evaluator is meant to return the names of all unbound variables in an expression. Callers like the form engine use it to work out which fields an expression depends on, so the expression is re-evaluated when those fields change.
Inside an arrow-function body, the names it returns are wrong:
a.map(x => f(b)), a.map(x => !b) and a.map(x => b.c) all return ["a"], missing f and/or b.

a.then(v => !isEmpty(b) ? v + 3 : v) returns ["a", ["v"], "isEmpty"]. That's a nested array that contains the arrow's own parameter, and b is missing.

Only bodies that are a plain binary or conditional expression come out right (e.g. a.map(x => x + b) returns ["a", "b"]). As a result, a field that's referenced only inside an arrow function is never registered as a dependency, and the expression isn't re-evaluated when that field changes. Callers also receive non-string entries even though the function promises a list of names.
Requested change
extractVariableNames() should return a flat list of strings with every unbound identifier in an arrow-function body. That includes identifiers in call arguments, unary operands, and member-expression objects. It should leave out the arrow's own parameters, and it should handle nested arrow functions.
Acceptance criteria
extractVariableNames('a.map(x => f(b))') returns a, f, and b.

extractVariableNames('a.then(v => !isEmpty(b) ? v + 3 : v)') returns a, isEmpty, and b, and never v.

The result never contains non-string entries.

Arrow-function parameters are excluded, including in nested arrow functions.

Unit tests in esm-expression-evaluator cover arrow bodies made of call, unary, member, binary, and conditional expressions, nested arrow functions, and parameter exclusion.

commits.subject: (fix) O3-6093: Improve support for arrow functions in expression variable extractor (#1943)

summary: Creating a new list from a patient's chart ("Add to list") doesn't take the user back to add the patient
description:
Repo: openmrs-esm-patient-management (patient-list-management-app)
Background
A user who opens Add to list from a patient's chart wants to put that patient on a list.

"Create new patient list" is only a step towards that when the list they need doesn't exist yet.

Creating the list isn't the goal. Adding the patient is.

Steps to reproduce
Open a patient's chart (e.g. Molly QA380 Test, 10004GT on test3).

Go to Actions → Add to list → Create new patient list.

Fill in the form and press Create list.

Actual
The user is taken out of the patient chart to Home → Patient lists.

The new list exists, but the patient isn't on it.

The flow ends there, and nothing prompts the user to finish the task.

To finish, the user has to go back to the chart, reopen Add to list, find the new list and tick it.

Cancel also leaves the user on the Patient lists page, away from the patient.

Expected
After Create list, the user is taken back to the Add patient to list modal. The list of patient lists is refreshed to include the new list, and the new list is checked.

The user can then click Save to add the patient, or uncheck the new list first if they need to.

Save adds the patient and confirms it, e.g. "Molly QA380 Test added to 'test'".

Why it matters
Leaving the user with an empty new list invites them to think the patient was added.

Lists created this way can stay empty.

Technical note
add-patient.modal.tsx:34-40 navigates to home/patient-lists?create=true and closes the modal, without passing the patient or a way back.

commits.subject: (fix) O3-6096: Return to Add patient to list modal after creating a new list (#2821)

summary: "Free text dosage" toggle labels are inverted in the drug order form
description:
Repo: openmrs-esm-patient-chart (esm-patient-medications-app)
Steps to reproduce
Open a patient chart with an active visit, then Order basket → Drug orders → Add → search a drug (e.g. Paracetamol 500mg) → Order form.

Look at the Free text dosage toggle while it is switched off (structured Dose / Route / Frequency fields showing).

Switch it on (the free-text dosage box appears).

Actual
Toggle switched off → label reads "On".

Toggle switched on → label reads "Off".

The same inversion appears in translations, e.g. French shows "Activé" while the toggle is off.

Expected
The label matches the toggle state: "Off" when free-text dosage is off, "On" when it is on.
Why it matters
A clinician who believes structured dosing is selected can end up typing into the free-text box instead. Example on test3: Mill QA Test (10003YW), ORD-499 (Zyrtec 10mg) was saved as a free-text order whose only instruction is "-5". It has no dose, route, frequency or duration, so it never expires and stays in Active Medications. In the Edit drug order screen the toggle reads "Off" while the free-text box is visible.
Cause and fix
esm-patient-medications-app/src/add-drug-order/drug-order-form.component.tsx:981-982 passes labelA={t('on', 'On')} and labelB={t('off', 'Off')}. Carbon's Toggle shows labelA when unchecked and labelB when checked (checked ? labelB : labelA), so the labels are swapped.
Fix: labelA={t('off', 'Off')} and labelB={t('on', 'On')}, plus a unit test asserting the label text in both states.

commits.subject: (fix) O3-6097: Fix inverted labels on the free text dosage toggle (#3793)

summary: Service Queues always shows “Scheduled for today” and “On time”
description:
When a patient row is expanded in Service Queues, the current-visit header always displays “Scheduled for today” and “On time” beneath the visit type. Neither label is derived from appointment data or a punctuality attribute. This presents unsupported scheduling information as fact, including for visits without that data.
Steps to reproduce
Open Service Queues and the Outpatient Clinic waiting list.

Expand a patient with a loaded current visit and no appointment/punctuality data.

Inspect the labels beneath the visit type.

Actual result
“Scheduled for today” and “On time” appear regardless of whether the visit has supporting scheduling or punctuality data.
Expected result
Only display scheduling and punctuality claims supported by actual data. When unavailable, omit the labels or show an explicitly unknown state. A visit start date alone does not establish an appointment or punctuality.
Evidence
Independently verified in the release-tagged source:
v12.0.0 current-visit-summary.component.tsx, lines 84–89: both translated labels render unconditionally once the visit is loaded.

v12.0.0 unit test: a fixture with only visitType and encounters, with no visit date or attributes, is expected to show both labels.

v11.1.0 baseline component: same unconditional labels.

Already documented under Service Queues Technical Reference — Known issues and caveats.

The current visit shows “Scheduled for today” and “On time”. Both labels appear without checking appointment or punctuality data.
Suggested fix and acceptance
Remove the unconditional labels until they can be backed by real scheduling/punctuality data. Update the unit test so a visit without that data does not claim “Scheduled for today” or “On time”. If data-derived labels are retained, cover supported and missing-data cases.

summary: Double-clicking Save and close creates duplicate vitals encounters
description:
Double-clicking Save and close can save the same vitals twice while the first request is still pending.
Steps to reproduce
Open a test patient with an active visit and select Record vitals.

Enter a temperature of 37 °C and a heart rate of 72.

Simulate a slow connection, then double-click Save and close. The recording uses a 750 ms delay on each outgoing encounter POST.

Reload Vitals & Biometrics.

Actual result
Two entries appear with the same measurements. The backend also contains two separate, non-voided vitals encounters for the same patient and visit.
Expected result
Save should stay disabled until the request finishes. Clicking it more than once should create only one encounter.
Tested versions
Reproduced locally with the published vitals modules 13.0.0 and 12.3.4, using the same 3.8.0 RC backend and surrounding frontend. This confirms the behavior also exists in the older vitals module; the full previous release was not tested.
Suggested fix
The save handler starts the request without returning its promise. Return or await it so isSubmitting stays true until the save finishes.
Add a test that double-clicks Save while the request is pending and checks that only one encounter is saved.

commits.subject: (fix) O3-6100: Prevent duplicate vitals saves (#3792)

summary: Extension config keys are reported as unknown before their module has loaded
description:
When an extension mounts before its module's bundle has loaded, the console logs Unknown config key '<module>.<key>' provided. Ignoring. for keys the module does declare in its schema. The value is still applied, so the warning is a false alarm, but it shows up on most pages and makes real config mistakes harder to spot.
O3-2287 fixed this for module config: computeModuleConfig waits until the module has loaded before it checks for unknown keys. computeExtensionConfig doesn't wait yet, so it still checks against the implicit schema every app gets from registerApp, and every declared key looks unknown.
Proposed fix, in https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core/pull/1946: skip the unknown-key check for extension config until the module has loaded, the same way module config does. Whether the module has loaded is part of the cache key, so a module that never defines a schema still gets checked once it loads. Wrong types and failing validators are still reported as before.
Steps to reproduce: configure a declared key for a module whose extension renders on a page the module isn't routed to (for example a homepage widget), then load that page and watch the console.

commits.subject: (fix) O3-6135: Don't report extension config keys as unknown before the module has loaded (#1946)
